summary: Steel fire-lookout tower on the summit in 1955; a 2004 survey found it gone, with a wooden observation platform built in its place.

facts.status_note: The steel tower was gone by the 2004 survey; a shorter wooden observation platform stood in its place.

access.note: Reached on the Pinchot Trail in Lackawanna State Forest; no source describes access to the summit platform.

visit.trail_note: Pinchot Trail in Lackawanna State Forest; the trailhead has ample parking.

events.note: NGS station description: steel fire-lookout tower about 90 ft high on the summit (described by Coast and Geodetic Survey 1955)
Found dismantled at the August 6, 2004 survey recovery; the removal date is not given

evidence.supports: steel fire-lookout tower about 90 ft high
evidence.quote: THE STATION IS A REGULAR STEEL FIRE-LOOKOUT TOWER ABOUT 90 FT. HIGH.

evidence.supports: tower on the summit of Big Pine Hill
evidence.quote: IT IS LOCATED ON THE SUMMIT OF BIG PINE HILL.
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1955 (IWS)

evidence.supports: station recovered in destroyed condition on August 6, 2004
evidence.quote: Recovered in Destroyed Condition on August 6, 2004
Rich and I discovered that the tower referred to in the description has been removed.

evidence.supports: wooden observation platform in its place, no value as a geodetic control point
evidence.quote: The steel fire tower was completely dismantled and removed, and a shorter wooden observation platform (which has no value as a geodetic control point) was constructed in its place.
but the station landmark was destroyed.

evidence.quote: an excellent vista from Big Pine Hill.

evidence.quote: The trailhead is located in a scenic pine grove with ample parking.

notes_for_editor: No source found gives the built year, operator, or cab-floor height. The NGS figure of about 90 ft is for the whole structure, so no height_m is recorded. The Forest Fire Lookout Association register lists a different site, Pine Hill Tower Site (Lackawanna County) at US 420 and PA 249, used about 1917 and removed in 1981; it was not confirmed to be this hill and is not merged. The AllTrails page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The access and trail claims rest on one hiking guide. No photos added.
